169|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
170|
171|### 6.1 The loop
172|
173|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
174|
175|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
176|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
177|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
178|- **Ending.**
179|
180|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
181|| --- | --- | --- |
182|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
183|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
184|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
185|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
186|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
187|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
188|| The same call a third time | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
189|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
190|
191|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
192|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
193|
194|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
195|
196|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped at 12 per session; a 13th read is refused with an error, and the loop continues.
197|
198|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
199|| --- | --- | --- |
200|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
201|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
202|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
203|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
204|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
205|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
206|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
207|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |

209|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
210|
211|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
212|
213|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
214|| --- | --- | --- |
215|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
216|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
217|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
218|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |

225|| `connectorInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |

235|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
236|
237|```json
238|{
239|  "incidentId": "string",
240|  "deployment": "string",
241|  "component": "string",
242|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
243|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
244|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
245|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
246|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
247|  "action": {
248|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
249|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
250|    "resource": "full resource name",
251|    "updateMask": ["field"],
252|    "patch": {},
253|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
254|  },
255|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
256|  "rollback": "string",
257|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
258|}
259|```
260|
261|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
262|
263|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
264|
265|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
266|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
267|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
268|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
269|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, and `resource` is the incident's component. `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
270|
271|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
272|
273|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
274|
275|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
276|| --- | --- |
277|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's last `connector.run.completed` entry before the trip |
278|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's last `job.run.completed` entry before the trip |
279|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result with `successful: false` |
280|| `schema_drift` | An `alert.ingested` entry that violates the tripped schema tripwire |
281|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry with `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
282|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
283|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |

285|### 6.6 Guardrails
286|
287|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
288|- **Budgets.** Per investigation session: 24 turns, 12 read calls, 400,000 tokens (input plus output, configurable). Two remediation attempts per incident.
289|- **Stuck detection.** The same tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time ends the session with reason `stuck`.
290|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
291|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
292|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
293|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff on 429; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
294|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

16|
17|## 1. Summary
18|
19|Fleet SRE is an agentic site reliability engineer for MSSPs running multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR. It writes each service's monitoring contract, investigates when a tripwire fires, proposes a fix for a human to approve, and amends the contract when an incident exposes a gap. The platform underneath exists only to give it safe tools and deterministic checks.
20|
21|- **Problem.** An MSSP runs many tenants (SOAR environments) across many services in one instance. Connectors fail silently, a `LIVE` status can sit on a connector that ingests nothing, and each tenant's monitoring depends on who onboarded it.
22|- **What the SRE does.** Authors one contract per service version, investigates incidents with read-only tools, proposes allowlisted actions, writes the postmortem and drafts contract amendments.
23|- **Why it can be trusted.** It isn't. Deterministic code grades every output: contracts by a chaos scorecard, evidence when it is recorded, diagnoses when they are submitted, fixes by tripwires.
24|- **Fleet leverage.** Amendments land on the service contract, so one tenant's incident hardens every tenant on that service.
25|- **Built on.** A local-first Python system with a mock SecOps built against Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format, deployed to a personal GCP project (Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, IAM, Cloud Run, Firestore).
26|- **Entry.** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie track, "Build for Your World" theme. Submission due 2026-11-04 at 9:00 PM ET.
27|
28|## 2. Design principles
29|
30|1. **Verified, not trusted.** Every SRE output has a deterministic check: a contract must pass the chaos scorecard, evidence must exist when it is recorded, a diagnosis must rest on recorded evidence of the right kind, a fix must pass change-point tripwires.
31|2. **Reason once, run cheap.** The model works when a contract is written or amended and when an incident opens. No model sits in the watch loop.
32|3. **One contract per service.** The contract versions with the service definition. Per-tenant differences are parameters. The platform uses whatever integration version is installed; upgrades are a separate process.
33|4. **Every incident hardens every tenant.** Amendments land on the service contract, so a gap found on one tenant closes for all of them.
34|5. **The agent holds no credentials.** Read tools are proxied by the platform under a read-only identity; writes need human approval and run under a separate identity. IAM enforces this and tests prove it.
35|6. **Built against Google's spec.** Mock resources and log labels copy the published Chronicle API and SOAR logging docs, so the mock can be swapped for a real instance. What is invented is labelled as invented (see `mocks.md` §9).
36|7. **Local first.** Everything runs on a laptop with `make demo`. GCP services are adapters behind ports, swapped in late.
37|8. **The same rule applies to the build.** Humans write what defines correctness (contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, acceptance test specs, SRE prompts in `prompts/`). The coding agent writes what is graded against them.
38|9. **Checks live inside the tools.** A gate runs inside the tool that moves work forward (recording evidence, submitting a diagnosis), never as a separate tool the model may choose to call, because a confident model skips optional checks. A refused call comes back as an error the model reads and fixes. The model chooses every call; code never hard-codes the order.
39|
40|Field lessons that shape the tripwires: absence-only detection cannot tell quiet from broken, and a field changing type (severity arriving as a string) passes every volume check.
41|
42|## 3. The SRE loop
43|
44|The model acts at three points (author, investigate, close). Deterministic code grades each output before anything changes; inside an investigation, the gates sit in the tools (§6.1).
45|
46|```mermaid
47|flowchart LR
48|  A["Write contract (SRE)"] --> B["Chaos scorecard"] --> C{"Passes?"}
49|  C -- "no: revise" --> A
50|  C -- "yes" --> D["Approve contract (human)"] --> E["Tripwires watch"]
51|  E -- "tripwire fires" --> F["Investigate (SRE)"]
52|  F -- "escalates or hits a limit" --> N["Needs input (human)"]
53|  N -- "reply, more turns, or fault state changed" --> F
54|  F -- "proposes action" --> G["Approve fix (human)"]
55|  G -- "rejected with notes" --> F
56|  G -- "approved" --> H["Apply fix (deployer identity)"] --> I{"Verified?"}
57|  F -- "no action: verify recovery" --> I
58|  I -- "no: retry, max 2, then escalate" --> F
59|  I -- "yes" --> J["Close incident (SRE postmortem)"]
60|  J -- "gap found: amend" --> A
61|```
62|
63|1. **Author.** Given a service brief, sample logs and parameters, the SRE drafts a contract. The harness scores it; the SRE revises against the scorecard (max 3 revisions); a human approves.
64|2. **Watch.** The evaluator runs every deployment's tripwires. No model call.
65|3. **Investigate.** A trip opens an incident. The SRE states hypotheses, investigates with read tools, records evidence that is checked as it is recorded, and submits a diagnosis through a gated tool (§6.1). The diagnosis proposes one action, proposes no action and asks for verification, or escalates.
66|4. **Hand off.** An escalation, or an investigation that hits a limit, pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT. No model calls are made while it waits. It resumes the same session only when something changed: a human replied, more turns were granted, or the incident's tripwire state changed (for example, a credential was rotated outside the platform).
67|5. **Approve and apply.** A human sees hypotheses, evidence and the patch diff, and approves or rejects with notes; notes go back to the SRE as its next message. On approval the executor journals its intent, then applies the change under the deployer identity.
68|6. **Verify.** A change-point window tightens checks on that component. The diagnosis states the expected outcome; the tripwires decide. Failure returns to investigation at most twice, then escalates.
69|7. **Close and learn.** The SRE writes a postmortem. If the incident exposed a gap (a late or missing trip), it drafts an amendment, which goes back through the scorecard and approval and then applies to every deployment of that service.
70|
71|## 4. The platform
72|
73|### 4.1 Domain model
74|
75|- **Service**: a versioned contract (components + tripwires). Two ship: `alert-ingestion` (connector instance + ETL flow) and `intel-sync` (job instance).
76|- **Deployment**: a service applied to one SOAR environment, with parameters. Adding a deployment arms its tripwires.
77|- **Component**: one Chronicle resource per deployment, found in logs by its labels.
78|- **Incident**: opened by a trip; holds the investigation session (hypotheses, recorded evidence, transcript), the diagnosis, approvals and rejections, executor journal records, the verification result and the postmortem.
79|
80|### 4.2 Ports and adapters
81|
82|| Port | Local adapter (D3–D6) | GCP adapter (D7) |
83|| --- | --- | --- |
84|| `LogSink` | JSONL file | Cloud Logging `entries.write` |
85|| `LogSource` | JSONL replay / tail | Pub/Sub push from a log sink |
86|| `LogQuery` (SRE `query_logs`) | Scan JSONL store | Cloud Logging `entries.list` |

94|
95|```mermaid
96|flowchart LR
97|  M["Mock SecOps (Cloud Run)"] -- logs --> L["Cloud Logging"] -- sink --> P["Pub/Sub"] -- push --> EV["Evaluator"]
98|  S["Cloud Scheduler"] -- tick --> EV
99|  EV -- "opens incident" --> SRE["SRE runtime"]

106|State (deployments, tripwire state, incidents, investigation sessions, approvals, executor journal, transcripts) lives in Firestore when deployed, SQLite locally. The evaluator needs a clock as well as events, because silence never arrives as a message.
107|
108|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
109|
110|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
111|
112|```json
113|{
114|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
115|  "version": "1.0.0",
116|  "parameters": {
117|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
118|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
119|  },
120|  "components": [
121|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
122|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
123|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
124|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
125|  ],
126|  "tripwires": [
127|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
128|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
129|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
130|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
131|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
132|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
133|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
134|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
135|  ],
136|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
137|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
138|}
139|```
140|
141|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
142|
143|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
144|
145|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
146|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
147|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`).
148|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, and its severity is the worst entry in it.
149|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
150|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
151|
152|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
153|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
154|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
155|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
156|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
157|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
158|
159|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.
160|
161|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
162|
163|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
164|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
165|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
166|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
167|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.
168|
169|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
170|
171|### 6.1 The loop
172|
173|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
174|
175|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
176|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
177|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
178|- **Ending.**
179|
180|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
181|| --- | --- | --- |
182|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
183|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
184|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
185|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
186|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
187|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
188|| The same call a third time | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
189|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
190|
191|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
192|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
193|
194|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
195|
196|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped at 12 per session; a 13th read is refused with an error, and the loop continues.
197|
198|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
199|| --- | --- | --- |
200|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
201|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
202|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
203|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
204|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
205|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
206|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
207|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
208|
209|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
210|
211|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
212|
213|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
214|| --- | --- | --- |
215|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
216|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
217|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
218|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |
219|
220|### 6.4 Action allowlist
221|
222|| Action | Notes |
223|| --- | --- |
224|| `connectorInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `intervalSeconds`, `parameters` |
225|| `connectorInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
226|| `connectorInstances.runOnDemand` | |
227|| `jobInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `parameters` |
228|| `jobInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
229|| `jobInstances.runOnDemand` | |
230|| `none` | No write: the fault has cleared (for example, after a human acted on an escalation). Goes straight to verification |
231|| `escalate` | Required when the fix is outside the allowlist (e.g. a credential rotation). Pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT |
232|
233|`connectorInstances.setLogsCollection` is not an action: turning on logging fixes nothing, so verification would fail it. The SRE can ask for it in an `escalationSummary`.
234|
235|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
236|
237|```json
238|{
239|  "incidentId": "string",
240|  "deployment": "string",
241|  "component": "string",
242|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
243|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
244|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
245|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
246|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
247|  "action": {
248|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
249|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
250|    "resource": "full resource name",
251|    "updateMask": ["field"],
252|    "patch": {},
253|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
254|  },
255|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
256|  "rollback": "string",
257|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
258|}
259|```
260|
261|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
262|
263|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
264|
265|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
266|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
267|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
268|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
269|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, and `resource` is the incident's component. `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
270|
271|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
272|
273|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
274|
275|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
276|| --- | --- |
277|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's last `connector.run.completed` entry before the trip |
278|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's last `job.run.completed` entry before the trip |
279|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result with `successful: false` |
280|| `schema_drift` | An `alert.ingested` entry that violates the tripped schema tripwire |
281|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry with `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
282|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
283|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |
284|
285|### 6.6 Guardrails
286|
287|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
288|- **Budgets.** Per investigation session: 24 turns, 12 read calls, 400,000 tokens (input plus output, configurable). Two remediation attempts per incident.
289|- **Stuck detection.** The same tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time ends the session with reason `stuck`.
290|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
291|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.

1|# Fleet SRE — Mock Inventory
2|
3|As of 2026-10-28. Companion to [`spec.md`](spec.md) (source of truth) and [`deliverables.md`](deliverables.md) (D3 builds everything here).
4|
5|Revised 2026-10-29 (night) before D3: Chronicle method bodies (§4.1), method permissions (§4.2) and connector log collection (§4.1) checked against Google's docs.
6|
7|The mock simulates only what the SRE, the evaluator and the executor touch. Everything below is either **faithful** (copied from Google's or Microsoft's published docs, with a URL) or **invented** (labelled, because the docs do not publish it). §9 lists which is which.
8|
9|---
10|
11|## 1. What is being simulated
12|
13|```
14|Fake Sentinel (one workspace per tenant) ──poll──▶ Connector runtime ──AlertInfo──▶ Ingestion (ETL)
15|        ▲                                               │                               │
16|        │ plant canary                                   ▼                               ▼
17|   Canary planter                              python-container logs           etl-container logs
18|                                                + ConnectorLog records          (correlation_id)
19|Fake TI feed ──▶ Job runtime (intel-sync) ──▶ python-container logs + JobInstanceLog records
20|
21|Mock Chronicle API (control plane): read, patch, run, test ◀── SRE read tools / Executor writes
22|Fault injector (/_chaos): changes world behaviour on a schedule or on request
23|```
24|
25|All of it runs in one Python process (`fleetsre.mock`), driven by a `World` object with an injectable `Clock` and a seeded RNG, so a scenario replays identically.
26|
27|## 2. Fleet
28|
29|| Environment | Display name | Services | Alert volume (`expectedAlertsPerHour`) | Notes |
30|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
31|| `alpha` | Alpha Corp | alert-ingestion, intel-sync | 120 | High volume |
32|| `bravo` | Bravo Health | alert-ingestion, intel-sync | 30 | Medium |
33|| `charlie` | Charlie Retail | alert-ingestion | 2 | Deliberately quiet; a naive "no alerts in 90 min" detector false-alarms here |
34|| `canary` | MSSP Canary | alert-ingestion | 0 organic | MSSP-owned canary tenant (production canary story) |
35|
36|Connector `intervalSeconds`: 60 for all (demo speed). Job `intervalSeconds`: 300 (docs minimum is 60). Defined in `fixtures/fleet.yaml` (D1). Tenant names are fictional.
37|
38|## 3. Components
39|
40|### 3.1 Fake Sentinel (upstream, invented transport, faithful payload)
41|
42|One simulated workspace per environment. The connector polls it.
43|
44|- **Payload shape** follows Microsoft Sentinel *Incidents – List*: `value[]` of incidents with `name`, `etag`, `type: "Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents"`, and `properties` including `title`, `description`, `severity`, `status`, `incidentNumber`, `createdTimeUtc`, `firstActivityTimeUtc`, `lastActivityTimeUtc`, `lastModifiedTimeUtc`, `providerName`, `providerIncidentId`, `labels`, `additionalData.alertsCount`. [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/securityinsights/incidents/list)
45|- **Severity values**: `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Informational`.
46|- **Path**: simplified to `/_upstream/{env}/incidents?since=<iso8601>` (invented). The real ARM path is not needed.
47|- **Auth**: fake token endpoint `/_upstream/{env}/token` taking a client secret; returns 401 when the credential fault is active (invented).
48|- **Volume**: Poisson arrivals at the environment's rate, seeded.
49|
50|### 3.2 Connector runtime (emulates the SOAR `python` container)
51|
52|One worker per connector instance. Every `intervalSeconds` (while `enabled` and not stalled):
53|
54|1. Get a token from the fake token endpoint using the instance's `Client Secret` parameter.
55|2. Fetch incidents since the stored checkpoint (dedupe by `providerIncidentId`).
56|3. Map each incident to an `AlertInfo` (faithful field names, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/soar/respond/ide/creating-a-custom-connector)):
57|   - `name` ← `properties.title`
58|   - `ticket_id` / `display_id` ← `properties.providerIncidentId`
59|   - `rule_generator` ← first label or `"Sentinel Analytics"` (must not be empty)
60|   - `priority` ← severity map: `High→80`, `Medium→60`, `Low→40`, `Informational→-1` (Google's scale is Informative −1, Low 40, Medium 60, High 80, Critical 100)
61|   - unknown severity → the `Unknown Severity Priority` parameter if set, **otherwise the raw string is passed through** (this is the severity-drift bug)
62|   - `device_vendor = "Microsoft"`, `device_product = "Azure Sentinel"`
63|   - `start_time` / `end_time` ← first/last activity (unix ms)
64|   - `environment` ← the instance's environment
65|   - `events` ← one event dict per incident with `device_product`
66|4. Hand alerts to ingestion.
67|5. Emit logs (see §5) and, while log collection is on (§4.1), append `ConnectorLog` records. Every run ends with `connector.run.completed`, including a run that failed; a failed run writes `connector.run.warning` or `connector.run.error` first (invented). So `dead-connector` measures whether the connector ran, and `connector-errors` whether it ran cleanly.
68|
69|**Swallowed failure (Green Liar).** On a 401 from upstream, the worker catches the exception, writes a `WARNING` log (and, while log collection is on, a `WARNING` ConnectorLog) ("Failed to authenticate to Sentinel workspace: 401 Unauthorized"), returns zero alerts and still emits `connector.run.completed`. Status stays `LIVE`.
70|
71|**Custom connector definition (invented — not the Marketplace integration's real parameters).**
72|
73|| Integration | `MockSentinel` (custom: true), version `1.0` |
74|| --- | --- |
75|| Connector | `Mock Sentinel Incidents Connector` |
76|| `productFieldName` / `eventFieldName` | `device_product` / `event_name` |
77|
78|Connector instance parameters (`ConnectorInstanceParameter`: `value`, `displayName`, `description`, `mandatory`, `advanced`, `type`):
79|
80|| displayName | type | mandatory | default |
81|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
82|| Tenant ID | STRING | yes | per env |
83|| Client ID | STRING | yes | per env |
84|| Client Secret | PASSWORD | yes | per env |
85|| Workspace Name | STRING | yes | per env |
86|| Max Incidents Per Cycle | INT | no | `50` |
87|| Unknown Severity Priority | INT | no | `""` (empty) |
88|
89|### 3.3 Ingestion (emulates the SOAR `etl` container)
90|
91|Receives `AlertInfo` objects. For each: assign a `correlation_id` (UUID4 from the seeded RNG), emit one `etl` log entry `alert.ingested` with the alert in `jsonPayload.alert` (fields: `name`, `ticket_id`, `rule_generator`, `priority`, `device_vendor`, `device_product`, `environment`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `canary`). Filtering etl logs by `correlation_id` traces one alert's ingestion, as Google documents. [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/secops/collect-secops-soar-logs)
92|
93|Ingestion does **not** validate `priority`; a string passes straight through (realistic, and the point of the schema tripwire).
94|
95|### 3.4 Job runtime (intel-sync)
96|
97|One worker per job instance. Every `intervalSeconds`: fetch indicators from a fake TI feed (`/_upstream/{env}/indicators?lookbackHours=N`), "sync" them, write a `python` log entry `job.run.completed` with `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` and `jsonPayload.status`, and append a `JobInstanceLog` (`status` `SUCCESS`/`ERROR`, `message`, `startTime`, `endTime`). Updates the job instance's `lastRunTime`, `lastRunStatus`, `nextScheduledRunTime`. A failed run writes `job.run.error` and then still ends with `job.run.completed` (`status: ERROR`, `indicatorsSynced: 0`, severity ERROR), so `dead-job` measures whether the job ran and `hollow-run` checks only `SUCCESS` runs (invented).
98|
99|Job definition (invented): integration `MockThreatIntel` v`1.0`, job `Sync Indicators`. Parameters:
100|
101|| displayName | type | mandatory | default |
102|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
103|| Feed URL | URL | yes | `/_upstream/{env}/indicators` |
104|| Lookback Hours | INT | yes | `24` |
105|
106|`Lookback Hours = 0` returns zero indicators with status `SUCCESS` (the hollow-success bug).
107|
108|### 3.5 Canary planter
109|
110|`POST /_upstream/{env}/incidents:plant` creates an incident whose title starts with `[CANARY]` and whose `providerIncidentId` is `canary-<uuid>`. Ingestion sets `jsonPayload.alert.canary = true` for it. A canary counts as seen when an `alert.ingested` entry has `alert.canary: true` and `alert.ticket_id` equal to the planted `providerIncidentId`. Canaries are planted with severity `Informational`, so F3 never affects them. The platform's synthetic tripwire calls this endpoint; in production it would target only the `canary` environment (spec §5).
111|
112|## 4. Mock Chronicle API (control plane)
113|
114|FastAPI app `fleetsre.mock.chronicle_api`. Google-style REST: base `/v1/`, resource names in the path, custom methods as `POST /v1/{name}:method`, `PATCH` with an `updateMask` query parameter, list with `pageSize` / `pageToken` returning `nextPageToken`. Errors use Google's shape: `{"error": {"code": 404, "message": "...", "status": "NOT_FOUND"}}`.
115|
116|Fixed prefix: `projects/fleet-sre-demo/locations/us/instances/mock-soar`.
117|
118|### 4.1 Resources, methods and fields
119|
120|Only these. Field lists are copied from the v1/v1beta reference; implement every listed field (populate with realistic values), add nothing.
121|
122|**environments** — `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/instances/{i}/environments/{environment}` — [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.environments)
123|- Methods: `get`, `list`, `create`
124|- Fields: `name`, `displayName`, `description`, `contact`, `contactEmails`, `contactPhone`, `base64Image`, `retentionDuration`, `dynamicParameters[]`, `system`, `aliasesJson`, `instanceUri`, `dataAccessScopesJson`, `weight`, `id`
125|
126|**integrationInstances** — `.../integrations/{integration}/integrationInstances/{instance}` — [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.integrations.integrationInstances)
127|- Methods: `get`, `list`, `executeTest`
128|- Fields: `name`, `environment`, `displayName`, `parameters[]` (`id`, `displayName`, `type`, `description`, `propertyName`, `mandatory`, `value`), `integrationIdentifier`, `identifier`, `description`, `configured`, `remote`, `agent`, `systemDefault`
129|- `executeTest`: empty request body; response `{"successful": bool, "message": string}` ([docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.integrations.integrationInstances/executeTest)). Calls the fake token endpoint with the environment's credential. Changes no state.
130|
131|**connectorInstances** — `.../integrations/{integration}/connectors/{connector}/connectorInstances/{connectorInstance}` — [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.integrations.connectors.connectorInstances)
132|- Methods: `get`, `list`, `create`, `patch`, `runOnDemand`, `setLogsCollection`
133|- Fields: `name`, `agent`, `environment`, `displayName`, `description`, `intervalSeconds`, `documentationLink`, `allowList[]`, `productFieldName`, `eventFieldName`, `timeoutSeconds`, `connectorDefinitionName`, `integrationVersion`, `version`, `loggingEnabledUntilUnixMs`, `statistics` (`pastDayAlertsCount`, `avgAlertsPerDay`), `parameters[]` (`value`, `displayName`, `description`, `mandatory`, `advanced`, `type`), `connectorId`, `identifier`, `id`, `updateAvailable`, `custom`, `enabled`, `remote`, `status` (`LIVE` | `NOT_LIVE`), `integration`
134|- `patch`: `integrationVersion` is required on patch (per docs); 400 without it. Every successful patch increments `version`.
135|- `runOnDemand`: request `{"connectorInstance": ConnectorInstance}` (required). Response `{"debugOutput": string, "success": bool, "sampleCases": [SampleCase]}`. `SampleCase` has `displayName`, `productName`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `eventCount`, `fullCaseInfoAsJson` ([docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1beta/projects.locations.instances.integrations.connectors.connectorInstances/runOnDemand)).
136|  - Mock: one extra run with the stored configuration. The body's values are not used (invented). The regular schedule is unchanged.
137|- `setLogsCollection`: request `{"enabled": bool}`; response `{"logEnableExpirationTime": "<unix ms>"}` ([docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.integrations.connectors.connectorInstances/setLogsCollection)).
138|  - `enabled: true` clears the instance's existing ConnectorLogs and starts a 3-hour collection period ([UI docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/soar/ingest/connectors/view-connector-logs)).
139|  - It sets `loggingEnabledUntilUnixMs` to the returned value.
140|  - `enabled: false` ends the period now.
141|- `PASSWORD` parameter values are returned as `"********"` (mock policy). A patch whose `PASSWORD` parameter value is `"********"` keeps the stored value (invented; makes GET → edit → PATCH safe).
142|- `status` semantics are not documented. Mock rule: `LIVE` while `enabled`, `NOT_LIVE` when disabled. Stalls and swallowed errors do not change it.

144|
145|**connectorInstances.logs** — `.../connectorInstances/{connectorInstance}/logs/{log}` — [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1beta/projects.locations.instances.integrations.connectors.connectorInstances.logs)

Mock: one extra run with the stored configuration.

159|**jobInstances.logs** — `.../jobInstances/{jobInstance}/logs/{log}` — [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.instances.integrations.jobs.jobInstances.logs)
160|- Methods: `get`, `list` (newest first)

166|### 4.2 Authorization
167|
168|Every request carries an identity. Local dev: header `X-Fleetsre-Identity: obs-reader|deployer` (only when `FLEETSRE_DEV_AUTH=1`). Deployed: Google ID token; the service-account email maps to an identity. Permission names follow the documented pattern `chronicle.<resource>.<verb>` (e.g. `chronicle.connectorInstanceLogs.get` is the documented permission for `logs.get`).
169|

185|## 5. Log format
186|
187|Every log line, local or in Cloud Logging, is a Cloud Logging `LogEntry`:
188|
189|```json
190|{
191|  "insertId": "a1b2c3d4e5",
192|  "timestamp": "2026-10-29T14:00:05.123Z",
193|  "severity": "WARNING",
194|  "logName": "projects/fleet-sre-demo/logs/chronicle-soar",
195|  "resource": {
196|    "type": "k8s_container",
197|    "labels": {
198|      "project_id": "fleet-sre-demo",
199|      "location": "us-central1",
200|      "cluster_name": "mock-soar",
201|      "namespace_name": "chronicle-soar",
202|      "pod_name": "python-0",
203|      "container_name": "python"
204|    }
205|  },
206|  "labels": {
207|    "integration_name": "MockSentinel",
208|    "integration_version": "1.0",
209|    "connector_name": "Mock Sentinel Incidents Connector",
210|    "connector_instance": "alpha-sentinel"
211|  },
212|  "jsonPayload": {
213|    "event": "connector.run.completed",
214|    "runId": "run-000123",
215|    "environment": "alpha",
216|    "alertsFetched": 0,
217|    "message": "Failed to authenticate to Sentinel workspace: 401 Unauthorized"
218|  }
219|}
220|```
221|
222|Faithful: `namespace_name = "chronicle-soar"`, `container_name` ∈ {`playbook`, `python`, `etl`}, and the entry `labels`: connector logs carry `integration_name`, `integration_version`, `connector_name`, `connector_instance`; job logs carry `integration_name`, `integration_version`, `job_name`; etl logs carry `correlation_id`. [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/secops/collect-secops-soar-logs)
223|
224|Invented: `logName`, `pod_name`, `cluster_name`, every `jsonPayload` field, and the `event` names below.
225|
226|| `event` | Container | Labels | Key payload fields |
227|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
228|| `connector.run.started` | python | connector | `runId`, `environment` |
229|| `connector.run.completed` | python | connector | `runId`, `alertsFetched`, `environment` |
230|| `connector.run.warning` | python | connector | `runId`, `message` (severity WARNING) |
231|| `connector.run.error` | python | connector | `runId`, `message` (severity ERROR) |
232|| `alert.ingested` | etl | `correlation_id` | `alert{...}`, `environment` |
233|| `job.run.completed` | python | job | `runId`, `status`, `indicatorsSynced`, `environment` |
234|| `job.run.error` | python | job | `runId`, `message` (severity ERROR) |
235|
236|Environment is not a documented log label. The platform maps `connector_instance` / `job_name` + environment through the API; the mock also puts `environment` in `jsonPayload` for convenience (invented).
237|
238|Local sink: append-only JSONL, one `LogEntry` per line, `insertId` unique per entry (seeded).
239|
240|`resource.labels.project_id` and the project in `logName` are read from `$PROJECT` at runtime, because Cloud Logging requires the real project ID (`docs/decisions/logging-resource.md`). `fleet-sre-demo` appears only in fake Chronicle resource names and in test fixtures.
241|
242|## 6. Fault catalog
243|
244|Each fault has a defined cause, what the native API shows, what should trip, and the **right answer**: the action a correct SRE takes. The right answers make the evaluations gradeable.
245|
246|| ID | Fault | Mock behaviour | Native API shows | Should trip | Right answer |
247|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
248|| F1 | `connector_stall` | Worker for one instance stops running. No logs, no ConnectorLogs | `status: LIVE`, `enabled: true` | `dead-connector` (cadence) | `connectorInstances.restart`. The mock clears a stall on any `enabled` false→true transition |
249|| F2 | `credential_expiry` | Upstream token endpoint returns 401 for one env. Connector swallows it: WARNING logs every run (and WARNING ConnectorLogs while log collection is on), zero alerts, runs on schedule | `status: LIVE`; `executeTest` → `successful: false`; the Logs tab is empty unless log collection is on | `connector-errors` (errorSignature), `canary` (synthetic) | `escalate`, category `credential_failure`. Siblings healthy → tenant-specific. Fix (rotate secret) is outside the allowlist |
250|| F3 | `severity_drift` | A fraction `rate` (fault `params`, e.g. 0.5) of new upstream incidents arrive with an unmapped severity (`"Critical"`); with `Unknown Severity Priority` empty, their `priority` becomes a string | `status: LIVE`, volume normal | `priority-shape` (schema) | `connectorInstances.patch` `parameters`: set `Unknown Severity Priority` to `100` (or `80`) |
251|| F4 | `job_hollow_success` | Job parameter `Lookback Hours` set to `0` (simulates a bad config change, visible in `tripwire_history` as a recent change); runs succeed with 0 indicators. Injection sets the parameter through the same path as a patch (bumps `updateTime`); `clear()` restores the value it replaced | `lastRunStatus: SUCCESS` | intel-sync `hollow-run` (schema on `indicatorsSynced > 0` over N runs) | `jobInstances.patch` `parameters`: `Lookback Hours` → `24` |
252|| F5 | `job_error` | Fake TI feed returns 500; job runs end `ERROR` | `lastRunStatus: ERROR` | intel-sync `job-errors` (errorSignature) | `escalate`, category `job_failing` (upstream outage) |
253|| F6 | `connector_flap` | Instance emits ERROR on a fraction `rate` of runs (fault `params`, e.g. 0.2 or 0.7). ERROR runs still fetch and ingest normally | `status: LIVE` | `connector-errors` only if threshold met | Harness-only scenarios for false-positive and threshold tuning |
254|| F7 | `job_stall` | Job worker stops running; `nextScheduledRunTime` goes stale | `lastRunStatus` unchanged, `enabled: true` | intel-sync `dead-job` (cadence) | `jobInstances.restart`, category `job_stalled`. The mock clears a job stall on any `enabled` false→true transition |
255|
256|Clearing: `DELETE /_chaos/faults/{id}` restores normal behaviour within 2 intervals. F2 has no allowlisted fix; in the demo, the admin UI "mark rotated" button clears it.
257|
258|## 7. Chaos API
259|
260|Enabled only when `FLEETSRE_CHAOS=1`; otherwise every `/_chaos` route returns 404.
261|
262|| Method | Path | Body | Effect |
263|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
264|| `POST` | `/_chaos/faults` | `{"type": "severity_drift", "environment": "alpha", "target": "<resource name, optional>", "params": {"rate": 0.5}}` | Activates a fault; returns `{"id": "..."}` |
265|| `GET` | `/_chaos/faults` | | Active faults |
266|| `DELETE` | `/_chaos/faults/{id}` | | Clears a fault |
267|| `POST` | `/_chaos/schedule` | list of `{at, type, environment, params?, clearAt?}` | Scenario schedule (harness and the live auto-chaos loop) |
268|

270|
271|- `World(seed, clock, sink, fleet)`; `world.step_until(t)` advances a `SimClock` and runs every due worker in timestamp order.
272|- Same seed + same fleet + same fault schedule → byte-identical JSONL.
273|- Wall-clock mode (`world.run_forever()`) is used for the live demo only.

{"content":""""D4 scorecard harness: score one contract against its scenarios."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from fleetsre.contracts import Contract
from fleetsre.harness.replay import ScenarioResult, run_scenario
from fleetsre.harness.scenario import Scenario


@dataclass
class Scorecard:
    results: list[ScenarioResult] = field(default_factory=list)
    passed: bool = False
    expected_hit_rate: float = 0.0
    false_positives: int = 0


def scorecard(
    contract: Contract, scenarios: list[Scenario]
) -> Scorecard:
    """Score one contract against its service's scenarios."""
    scored = [s for s in scenarios if s.service == contract.service]
    results = [run_scenario(contract, scenario) for scenario in scored]
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    for scenario, result in zip(scored, results):
        items = (
            len(scenario.expected.trips)
            + len(scenario.expected.recoveries)
            + len(scenario.expected.mustNotTrip)
        )
        total += items
        violated = 0
        for rule in scenario.expected.mustNotTrip:
            dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{rule.deployment}"
            if any(
                event.deployment == dep_id
                and (rule.tripwire == "*" or event.tripwire == rule.tripwire)
                for event in result.actual
            ):
                violated += 1
        hit += items - len(result.missing) - violated
    rate = hit / total if total else 1.0
    return Scorecard(
        results=results,
        passed=all(result.passed for result in results),
        expected_hit_rate=rate,
        false_positives=sum(len(result.unexpected) for result in results),
    )

from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
from fleetsre.mock.fleet import load_fleet
from fleetsre.mock.world import World, FaultSpec
from fleetsre.ports import MemorySink
T0 = datetime(2026,10,29,14,0,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
fleet = load_fleet('fixtures/fleet.yaml')
clock = SimClock(T0); sink = MemorySink()
world = World(fleet, 106, clock, sink)
world.schedule([{'at': 630, 'type': 'connector_flap', 'environment': 'alpha', 'params': {'rate': 0.7}}])
world.step_until(T0 + timedelta(seconds=7200))
# per-run worst severity for alpha connector runs in time order
runs = {}
order = []
for e in sink.entries:
    if e.jsonPayload.get('environment') != 'alpha': continue
    if e.resource.labels.get('container_name') != 'python': continue
    r = e.jsonPayload.get('runId')
    if not r: continue
    rank = {'DEBUG':0,'INFO':1,'NOTICE':2,'WARNING':3,'ERROR':4,'CRITICAL':5,'ALERT':6,'EMERGENCY':7}.get(e.severity,-1)
    if r not in runs: runs[r]=(e.timestamp,rank); order.append(r)
    else:
        ts, rk = runs[r]
        if rank > rk: runs[r]=(ts,rank)
seq = [(runs[r][0], runs[r][1]) for r in order]
seq.sort()
bad = [1 if rk>=3 else 0 for _,rk in seq]
print('total runs:', len(bad))
# trailing-10 bad counts
import itertools
trail = [sum(bad[max(0,i-9):i+1]) for i in range(len(bad))]
first_trip = next(i for i,c in enumerate(trail) if c>=8)
print('first trip run idx:', first_trip, 'at', seq[first_trip][0].isoformat())
post = trail[first_trip:]
dips = sum(1 for c in post if c<8)
print('post-trip windows below 8:', dips, 'of', len(post))
# consecutive-clean runs of length>=3 post first-trip?
maxclean=0; cur=0; occur=0
for b in bad[first_trip:]:
    if b==0: cur+=1; maxclean=max(maxclean,cur)
    else:
        if cur>=3: occur+=1
        cur=0
if cur>=3: occur+=1
print('max consec clean post-trip:', maxclean, 'occurrences of 3+ clean:', occur)
print('bad-run fraction:', sum(bad)/len(bad))
"","description":"Analyze flap-severe run sequence","yield_time_ms":60000}

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

{"content":""""Unit tests for D4 errorSignature recovery semantics pinned by the goal.

Acceptance T7 feeds only clean runs after a trip, so it cannot tell
window-based recovery ("window drops below threshold") from streak-based
recovery ("window-threshold+1 consecutive clean runs"). The flap-severe
reference scenario (70% ERROR runs, one trip, no recoveries) requires the
streak: the trailing window dips below threshold dozens of times while no
three consecutive clean runs ever occur.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
from fleetsre.contracts import load_contract
from fleetsre.evaluator.engine import Evaluator, TripEvent
from fleetsre.logmodel import LogEntry, MonitoredResource
from fleetsre.mock.fleet import load_fleet
from fleetsre.registry import Deployment

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 29, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

_DEP = "alert-ingestion/alpha"
_TW = "connector-errors"


def _evaluator(clock: SimClock) -> Evaluator:
    contract = load_contract(ROOT / "contracts" / "alert-ingestion.json")
    fleet = load_fleet(ROOT / "fixtures" / "fleet.yaml")
    params = dict(fleet.environments["alpha"].deployments["alert-ingestion"].parameters)
    return Evaluator(
        [contract],
        [Deployment(id=_DEP, service="alert-ingestion", environment="alpha", parameters=params)],
        clock,
    )


def _entry(ts: datetime, insert_id: str, event: str, run: str, severity: str) -> LogEntry:
    return LogEntry(
        insertId=insert_id,
        timestamp=ts,
        severity=severity,
        logName="projects/fleet-sre-demo/logs/chronicle-soar",
        resource=MonitoredResource(
            type="k8s_container",
            labels={
                "project_id": "fleet-sre-demo",
                "location": "us-central1",
                "cluster_name": "mock-soar",
                "namespace_name": "chronicle-soar",
                "pod_name": "python-0",
                "container_name": "python",
            },
        ),
        labels={
            "integration_name": "MockSentinel",
            "integration_version": "1.0",
            "connector_name": "Mock Sentinel Incidents Connector",
            "connector_instance": "alpha-sentinel",
        },
        jsonPayload={"event": event, "runId": run, "environment": "alpha"},
    )


def _feed(evaluator: Evaluator, clock: SimClock, entries: list[LogEntry]) -> list[TripEvent]:
    out: list[TripEvent] = []
    for entry in entries:
        clock.set(entry.timestamp)
        out.extend(evaluator.ingest(entry))
    out.extend(evaluator.tick())
    return out


def _run_entries(index: int, bad: bool) -> list[LogEntry]:
    base = T0 + timedelta(seconds=100 * index)
    run = f"unit-err-run-{index:04d}"
    entries = []
    if bad:
        entries.append(_entry(base, f"unit-err-w-{index:04d}", "connector.run.warning", run, "WARNING"))
    entries.append(
        _entry(base + timedelta(seconds=1), f"unit-err-d-{index:04d}", "connector.run.completed", run, "INFO")
    )
    return entries


def test_no_recovery_while_window_hovers_at_threshold() -> None:
    """Window dips below threshold without 3 consecutive clean runs: no recovery."""
    clock = SimClock(T0)
    evaluator = _evaluator(clock)
    for i in range(8):
        events = _feed(evaluator, clock, _run_entries(i, bad=True))
    trips = [e for e in events if e.kind == "trip" and e.tripwire == _TW]
    assert len(trips) == 1
    assert evaluator.status()[_DEP][_TW] == "tripped"
    # Hover: pairs of clean runs separated by bad ones. The trailing-10
    # window drops to 6-7 bad, but no 3 consecutive clean runs occur.
    pattern = [False, False, True] * 4
    for offset, bad in enumerate(pattern):
        events = _feed(evaluator, clock, _run_entries(100 + offset, bad=bad))
        assert [e for e in events if e.tripwire == _TW] == []
    assert evaluator.status()[_DEP][_TW] == "tripped"
    # Three consecutive clean runs recover exactly once.
    for offset in range(3):
        events = _feed(evaluator, clock, _run_entries(200 + offset, bad=False))
        recs = [e for e in events if e.kind == "recovery" and e.tripwire == _TW]
        if offset < 2:
            assert recs == []
        else:
            assert len(recs) == 1
    assert evaluator.status()[_DEP][_TW] == "ok"


def test_runs_judged_at_completion() -> None:
    """Warnings alone never trip; the trip fires when the runs complete."""
    clock = SimClock(T0)
    evaluator = _evaluator(clock)
    warns = []
    for i in range(8):
        warns.extend(_run_entries(i, bad=True)[:1])
    assert _feed(evaluator, clock, warns) == []
    assert evaluator.status()[_DEP][_TW] == "ok"
    dones = []
    for i in range(8):
        done = _run_entries(i, bad=True)[1]
        dones.append(done)
    events = _feed(evaluator, clock, dones)
    trips = [e for e in events if e.kind == "trip" and e.tripwire == _TW]
    assert len(trips) == 1
    assert evaluator.status()[_DEP][_TW] == "tripped"

## T10: test-side bug (protected path, needs your fix)

T10 fails at `tests/acceptance/d4/test_d4.py:1782`, `assert arrival_entries != stamp_order`, before any evaluator code runs in that block. It is mathematically impossible: the world emits all entries on a 60 s grid (verified: 648 entries, 60 distinct timestamps, min gap exactly 60 s), delays are `random() * 60 < 60`, so arrival order always equals timestamp order and the stable re-sort is the identity. The `inverted` assert below it is likewise unpassable. T10's part 1 (deterministic OOO cadence) passes, and I verified its intent manually: zero events under 60 s displacement for both services. Suggested test fix: shuffle with delays that can exceed the grid (or compare against sink order), then keep the `collected == []` assert, which my implementation satisfies.

## Decisions beyond A–I

1. **errorSignature recovery = `windowRuns − threshold + 1` consecutive clean runs** (3 for connector-errors), not "window drops below threshold". T7 and the golden fixture fit both, but `flap-severe` (70% errors, one trip, zero recoveries expected) is unpassable under window recovery — the trailing-10 dips below 8 in 36 of 63 post-trip windows (measured), flapping 42 events. Under streak recovery seed 106 has zero 3-clean streaks post-trip (measured), giving exactly one trip. Pinned by new `tests/unit/d4/test_error_recovery.py`.
2. **Runs are judged at completion**: trip/recovery evaluation runs on the component's cadence heartbeat event (contract-driven, falls back to every entry); run state still updates on every entry. This stops intra-run flapping (a run born clean at `started`, turning bad at its error entry).
3. Strict `>` for cadence-due and canary-missed boundaries (tests probe ±1 s only; goldens pass with margin).
4. Scorecard `expected_hit_rate` counts `mustNotTrip` entries as expected items — required, since the `hollow-no-where` mutant otherwise scores 1.0 (it only adds an unexpected trip).

Files changed: `fleetsre/evaluator/{tripwires,engine,canary}.py`, `fleetsre/harness/{replay,scorecard}.py`, `fleetsre/registry.py`, plus `tests/unit/d4/test_error_recovery.py`.
